questions.q: What is Python, in relation to Power BI?
options: A general-purpose programming language that Power BI happens to know how to run — not a Power BI feature or Microsoft product
A Microsoft-built extension of DAX
A replacement for the entire Power BI application
A file format Power BI uses to save reports
questions.explain: Python is a real, general-purpose language used far beyond Power BI. Power BI can run Python scripts, but Python wasn't built for Power BI the way Power Query and DAX were.

questions.q: How do Power Query and DAX differ from Python, in terms of what they were built for?
options: Power Query and DAX were purpose-built for Power BI; Python is a general-purpose language not built for Power BI at all
All three were built specifically for Power BI
Python was built for Power BI before Power Query or DAX existed
There is no meaningful difference between the three
questions.explain: Every Power Query step and DAX function exists because Power BI needed it. Python's strength inside Power BI comes precisely from being a general-purpose tool that wasn't designed around Power BI's constraints.

questions.q: What are the two specific places Python plugs into Power BI?
options: As a data source (via Get Data → Python script) and as a visual (the Python visual)
Inside every DAX measure and inside every Power Query step
Only as a replacement for the entire Power Query engine
Only inside the Power BI service, never in Desktop
questions.explain: Python has exactly two entry points in Power BI: producing a DataFrame as a data source (Lesson 18) and drawing a Matplotlib chart as a Python visual (Lesson 19) — not a general-purpose tool available everywhere.

questions.q: Why can't Python replace DAX for report-level calculations?
options: DAX measures recalculate live per filter context as a user interacts with a report; a Python script runs once and produces a static result
Python doesn't support any mathematical operations
DAX and Python actually do the exact same thing, so replacement doesn't matter
Power BI technically forbids Python from performing any calculations
questions.explain: DAX's core purpose is responding live to user interaction (slicers, filters, clicks). A Python script runs once at import or refresh time — it has no mechanism to recalculate per interaction the way DAX does.

questions.q: What is the scope of this 20-lesson course, according to Lesson 1?
options: Just enough Python and Pandas to be useful inside Power BI specifically — not a general software engineering or Python programming course
A complete general-purpose Python programming bootcamp
Exclusively machine learning and statistics in Python
How to replace Power Query and DAX entirely with Python
questions.explain: The course is deliberately scoped to reading, cleaning, and reshaping data with Pandas for the two places Python integrates with Power BI — general software engineering concepts are explicitly out of scope.
